# PPC Constraint Contract

## Status and authority boundary

This contract matures constraints only. It grants no implementation authority, does not authorize the candidate, does not alter `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json`, and cannot start Argo, publication, enrollment, or product implementation.

- approved design: `sha256:1a0d7b96fb4d4a35313355846a205bfd7c0f6c9fa093c957ba186f5b1bac0ba6`

The repository verifier re-derived 300 of 301 checks, but its temporary-directory fixture failed with `EROFS` in the read-only workshop environment. This contract therefore does not claim an exit-0 repository verification run.

## Closed behavioral model

The only production path is:

```text
controller dossier
  → validated canonical input artifact
  → validated pinned policy
  → bounded repository scan and monotonic reconciliation
  → compiled profile and exact production sources
  → read-only workshop context
  → controller-minted verification nodes and Merkle plan
  → disk-only proposal reconstruction and V2 policy certificate
  → separately authorized build
  → ordinary-node settlement
  → controller-owned process-evidence frontier
  → registered verification-node settlement
  → final disk-only profile reclassification
  → generic ledger verification and done()
  → bounded publication and lifecycle evidence
```

No model owns profile facts, signal resolutions, policy, applicability, expected outcomes, registered executables, waivers, acceptance, dogfood status, or enrollment.

### Production lifecycle state machine

The closed state set is exactly:

```text
LEGACY_INACTIVE
ACTIVE_UNPREPARED
INPUT_RECORDED
COMPILED
WORKSHOP_COMPLETE
PLANNED
GATE_PASSED
AUTHORIZED_BUILD
ORDINARY_SETTLED
EVIDENCE_FRONTIER_PREPARED
VERIFICATION_SETTLED
FINAL_PROFILE_PASSED
DONE
```

`LEGACY_INACTIVE` is the all-false legacy state and has no transition into the active path. Active transitions are exactly:

```text
ACTIVE_UNPREPARED --RECORD_INPUT--> INPUT_RECORDED
INPUT_RECORDED --COMPILE--> COMPILED
COMPILED --COMPLETE_WORKSHOP--> WORKSHOP_COMPLETE
WORKSHOP_COMPLETE --RECORD_PLAN--> PLANNED
PLANNED --PASS_GATE--> GATE_PASSED
GATE_PASSED --AUTHORIZE_BUILD--> AUTHORIZED_BUILD
AUTHORIZED_BUILD --SETTLE_ORDINARY--> ORDINARY_SETTLED
ORDINARY_SETTLED --PREPARE_EVIDENCE_FRONTIER--> EVIDENCE_FRONTIER_PREPARED
EVIDENCE_FRONTIER_PREPARED --SETTLE_VERIFICATION--> VERIFICATION_SETTLED
VERIFICATION_SETTLED --PASS_FINAL_PROFILE--> FINAL_PROFILE_PASSED
FINAL_PROFILE_PASSED --COMPLETE--> DONE
```

Every transition requires independently re-read and recomputed durable references. Unknown, skipped, repeated, reversed, or post-`DONE` transitions fail. A blocker or cannot-run result seals the invocation. Semantic drift or production `respec` yields `new-revision-required` and fresh planning and authorization; it never mutates an authorized plan in place.

### Trust boundaries

| Principal or input | Trusted for | Never trusted for |
|---|---|---|
| The Eye/controller | Dossier facts, signal resolutions, policy selection, approval, acceptance, enrollment | Executable evidence without independent checks |
| Models/workshop seats | Implementation and advisory review within fixed context | Applicability, waivers, production nodes, expected results, discharge, authorization |
| Repository files | Exact bytes after stable bounded reads | Business meaning from arbitrary text; safe paths from lexical checks alone |
| Structured detectors | Closed fact mappings owned by policy | Semantics for unknown dependencies or formats |
| Text scanners | Classification signals | Confirmed facts or suppression of dossier declarations |
| Policy and registry files | Rules and executables only after schema and content-address verification | Mutable labels, remote packs, caller-selected commands or outcomes |
| Proposal artifacts and ledgers | Durable evidence after hash, signature, chain, and proposal-binding verification | Stored state labels or producer summaries by themselves |
| Runtime adapter | Mapping closed semantic operations to host routes | Expected status, denial semantics, external URLs, or fixture-only pass logic |
| Structural artifacts | Bounded machine-readable relationships | Deployment effectiveness or operational outcomes |
| Process signers and records | Bounded signed activity at one plan/build/check identity | Perpetual freshness, legal compliance, or universal effectiveness |
| Filesystem, child process, loopback service | Results only after containment, stable-read, environment, limit, and endpoint checks | Best-effort fallback after unsafe or unavailable operations |
| Demo/self summaries and acceptance records | Evidence locators | Their own asserted success |

### Normative schema and identity rules

All controller, policy, registry, source, obligation, certificate, evidence, settlement, and publication objects are closed: missing or additional keys fail. Set-like arrays are non-empty where required, duplicate-free, code-unit sorted, and use exclusive `none` semantics. Controller strings must already be NFC. JSON trust boundaries reject duplicate keys, prototype keys, malformed UTF-8, trailing content, unsafe integers, non-finite values, unpaired surrogates, and non-plain structures.

Activation is mandatory when any of these is true: `proposal_lifecycle === true`, `market_bound === true`, `production_profile` is present, or `production_evidence` is present. An activated build requires both `proposal_lifecycle === true` and a complete profile before any model call. An all-false legacy build retains byte-compatible behavior and reports `production_profile_evaluated: false`.

The controller input contains exactly `build_context`, `production_profile`, and `production_evidence`. The profile retains every closed field and cross-field rule in the frozen frame. The additive Eye ruling creates exactly one additional profile fact, `file_ingress_formats`, whose value is `['none']` or a sorted non-empty subset of `['csv','json','xlsx']`; images are unsupported, unsafe XLSX rejects the complete workbook, and accepted files and extracted values inherit the complete top-level data-classification set.

The policy catalog is exactly the approved 31 IDs plus `FILE-INGRESS-001`, for 32 IDs total:

```text
AI-CLAIM-001 AI-DECISION-001 AI-EGRESS-001 AI-LINEAGE-001
AI-OPS-001 AI-OUTPUT-001 AI-PROVIDER-001 AI-RAG-001
AI-TENANT-001 AI-TOOL-001 AUTHN-001 AUTHN-002 AUTHZ-001 AUTHZ-002
DATA-001 DATA-002 DELIVERY-001 DELIVERY-002 FILE-INGRESS-001
OBS-001 OBS-002 PAY-001 PAY-002 PRIV-001 PRIV-002 PRIV-003
RECOVERY-001 RECOVERY-002 SCALE-001 SCALE-002 SUPPLY-001 SUPPLY-002
```

The eleven domains and eight check kinds remain closed. The check kinds are exactly:

```text
production-loopback-http-v1
production-auth-boundary-v1
production-tenant-isolation-v1
production-rate-limit-v1
production-webhook-v1
production-ai-egress-v1
production-json-assertions-v1
production-record-v1
```

For canonical JSON `H(x) = sha256(canonicalize(x))`. Required identities include:

```text
production_input_ref = H(canonical production input)
profile_ref = H({compiler_contract, compiled_profile})
repo_facts_ref = H({facts_version, sorted semantic facts, sorted resolved signals})
policy_ref = H(canonical policy)
registry_ref = H(sorted registry contracts and implementation identities)
runtime_manifest_ref = H(canonical validated runtime manifest) or null
process_keyring_ref = H(canonical public keyring) or null
evidence_config_ref = H({canonical evidence, runtime_manifest_ref, process_keyring_ref})
obligation_set_ref = H(sorted production source_ref values)
settlement_ref = H(canonical settlement result)
```

The global `plan_hash` binds the complete production input, compiled profile, semantic repository facts, policy, registry, evidence configuration, source set, obligations, discharge tests, and lifecycle metadata. Rule-local projections determine verification-node identity; every compiled-profile or policy-catalog change still changes global authorization.

### Failure semantics

| Condition | Public outcome |
|---|---|
| Successful compiler/verification | CLI exit `0` |
| Deterministic invalidity, contradiction, missing evidence, unresolved classification, or drift | CLI exit `2` |
| Unsafe/unavailable I/O, policy/registry failure, containment failure, race, or internal failure | CLI exit `1`; takes precedence over blockers |
| Registered assertion proves required result | Check exit `0` |
| Registered assertion ran and failed | Check exit `1` |
| Registered check could not run safely | Check exit `2` |
| `PROFILE_ESCALATED` only | Advisory; may accompany exit `0` |
| Any non-zero verification-node result | Obligation remains undischarged |

Compiler/lifecycle surfaces use exactly the 20 frozen `FINDING_CODES`. Publication recovery uses exactly its separate five-code vocabulary. The vocabularies cannot be merged or substituted. Internal detail such as `ATOMIC_REPLACEMENT_INDETERMINATE` is carried only beneath public `CANNOT_RUN`.

A failed operation before rename never replaces a valid output. Rename followed by failed parent-directory fsync returns cannot-run, advances no lifecycle state, and permits only exact old/new restart reconciliation. Missing, partial, or third-party bytes remain cannot-run.

## Non-claims preserved

A green result proves only its bounded executable predicates. It is not certification of security, availability, scalability, fairness, accuracy, legal compliance, complete data discovery, complete SBOM coverage, or operational effectiveness. Structural evidence proves only inspected artifacts; process evidence proves only a current authorized signature over bound records; runtime evidence proves only the bounded tested scenario. TELOS and the build controller remain one trust principal unless a later authorized design separates them.
